column1: # Game profile of Guns, Gore & Cannoli 2 (Switch: one package, build v0, its control data's display version 1.0.0 although the
# dump's file name says 1.0.4). Plays on the Mac
# Unity 5.6.6f2 (IL2CPP), SDK 3.8.0, NVN: the shaders are Shader objects in the player's serialized files (Data/*.assets and
# Data/Resources/unity default resources, the latter written by Unity 5.6.4p1). None of them carries type trees and no bundle
# supplies one, so their layout is written out in unityfs.py (SHADER_5_6, hash a70f7abc...).
# The dump this profile was brought up on is a Chinese-localised release (its UI strings are Chinese in Data/resources.assets,
# and no English counterpart of them), while its control data declares nine languages and no Chinese; see the game note.

# Game name: only a label for profile listings and the Mac window title; the iOS app name is the game name in the base NSP, and the bundle ID comes from the base game title ID (build_ipa.sh / NSP script)
# load order as on Horizon: main, subsdk*, sdk (subsdk0 = NintendoSDK_movie)
# The NPDM declares no system resource, so the game has no virtual address memory: Unity sets its heap to the application pool minus the used memory
# (3.14 GB in a 3.25 GB heap region, as the host reports it) and allocates from there. The block is 256 MB in front + 256 MB alias region + 256 MB
# the NPDM declares 0 MB of system resource (IsVirtualAddressMemoryEnabled off)
# the rewritten modules take 70 MB (main 46.9, sdk 14.2, subsdk0 5.5), more than the default 64 MB of used memory
# ---- Shader split (shader_split.py; Unity Shader objects, read by unityfs.py) ----
